---
title: "MLP"
---

The MLP (MultiLayer Perceptron) or *feedforward neural network* is Metis's most basic architecture.

## When this might be a good fit

The MLP is a good starting point for datasets with only static inputs. It is very fast to train and generate predictions from. Its relative accuracy depends on the bank and tuning. Unlike normalising flow or flow matching, it produces a deterministic trajectory.

## How does an MLP work?

### Architectural walkthrough
An MLP's computation is a series of matrix multiplications composed with non-linear activations. Metis's implementation also includes *residual* connections which stabilise the training of deeper networks.

In order to get a better sense of how these components work lets trace through the network's forward computation:


```python
x = self.input_layer(inputs)
for block in self.blocks:
    x = block(x)
x = self.output_layer(x)
```

The input_layer linearly projects (i.e. a matrix multiplication) the static input vector to vectors the size of the model's hidden dimension. Next, we iteratively pass our transformed inputs through a series of residual blocks.

Each residual block applies several layers to the input and adds the result back to the original input:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Residual block structure."
flowchart LR
    x[x] --> layer1[Linear]
    layer1 --> activation1[ReLU]
    activation1 --> dots[...]
    dots --> layerN[Linear]
    x --> add["\+"]
    layerN --> add
    add --> out[output]
```

Finally, the output layer linearly projects `x` to the output dimensionality.

### Training
The MLP is trained to minimise the Mean-Squared Error:

$$
\mathrm{Loss} = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}(\mathrm{MLP}^{\theta}(\mathrm{static\_input}_m)-\mathrm{output}_m)^2
$$

## Configuring an MLP

The installed preset is `model=mlp`: width `hidden_dim=64`, `num_blocks=2`
residual blocks and `num_layers_per_block=2`. Larger widths increase capacity
and memory; more blocks/layers deepen the mapping. The input size and flattened
`T × C` output size come from the dataset.

```bash
uv run metis train model=mlp model.model_options.hidden_dim=128 model.model_options.num_blocks=4
```

The Python equivalent is `Surrogate("mlp", model_options={"hidden_dim": 128,
"num_blocks": 4})`. Start with the small preset and compare validation error
before increasing capacity. The historical small/default/large names are mapped
in [migration](../package/migration.qmd).
